situation:
You are to assume the role of premium sales manager for the CALDER BAY LANCERS, a professional lacrosse franchise that plays eighteen home dates at a downtown arena. The club president (judge) has asked you to recommend what should happen to the arena's club lounge for the rest of this season, and to be ready to explain your reasoning.

The LANCERS merged their front office with a neighboring indoor lacrosse club last winter and have not finished digesting it. Two season ticket bases now sit in one database with two different benefit sets. Seats sold by the LANCERS have never included the club lounge, while every seat inherited from the other club was sold with lounge access on game nights written into the renewal letter.

The lounge is the strongest part of the in-venue experience the club sells beyond the game itself, and premium buyers ask about it before they ask about the seats. CROSSWIND HOSPITALITY GROUP, which runs private events at three venues nearby, is booking private events elsewhere and wants to book the lounge for corporate buyouts on eleven game nights this quarter. Those bookings would close the club's quarterly sales target on their own.

Taking the bookings means the inherited season ticket holders lose the lounge access their renewal letter promised, in the same weeks their renewal invoices go out. Keeping the lounge open to every season ticket holder on game nights means missing the quarterly sales target and letting CROSSWIND HOSPITALITY GROUP take those corporate buyouts to another venue for the rest of the season. The club president (judge) wants a recommendation on which way to go.

Be ready to explain what the lounge does for the club's competitive advantage, how a lounge that seats far fewer people than the number who now claim it should be sold, and what your recommendation does to renewals. The club president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
